Article Title: 'Conjecture and preconceived': SC refuses to rejig panel probing police action during CJP protest
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to reconstitute a five-member high-powered committee set up to probe alleged police excesses against student protesters in Delhi, saying that the committee was formed with the highest standards of fairness and transparency.This comes after a plea was filed in the apex court alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” even before it had commenced its enquiry."We are not inclined to effect any alteration in the constitution of the Committee, particularly where the prayer for such reconstitution proceeds on nothing more than conjecture and preconceived notions, articulated even before the HPEC has embarked upon its enquiry," the bench said."With respect to the concerns voiced over the treatment of witnesses and of those who may wish to come forward before the HPEC to furnish their account and voice their grievances, we request the HPEC that such vulnerable witnesses be extended due protection and their identities be kept confidential and undisclosed," it added.The bench directed that Senior Advocate Monika Gusain, along with advocate C Solomon, shall assist it as a representative of the HPEC, and shall further act as an independent arbiter between the parties."Similarly, we also request the HPEC to appoint a member secretary at the earliest, so as to facilitate any such logistical or other secretarial assistance as the HPEC may require in the discharge of its functions," the bench said.Earlier, advocate Prashant Bhushan raised doubts over one of the members of the panel, who was a former DGP of a northeastern state, and said he was under a "conflict of interest" as he was a close friend of a high functionary who was likely to be under investigation.Bhushan's views were backed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, however, opposed the reconstitution of the committee and urged the apex court to ignore such allegations.The apex court formed the HPEC, headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy, to examine allegations of police excesses against student protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest march on July 20 in Delhi and violence against police personnel.The committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana high court chief justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya DGP L R Bishnoi."This HPEC has been constituted bearing in mind a wide variety of considerations, including the individual expertise and experience of each of its members, as well as the diversity of the committee, among other factors," the bench had said.The July 20 march saw clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and teargas shells to disperse crowds.
Article Summary: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed that the allegations against the panel were based on “conjecture and preconceived notions” This comes after a plea was filed alleging that one of the members of the committee was a close friend of a high functionary who is involved in the matter.

Article Title: SC junks ex-Delhi mayor's plea for FIR on UP cops
Article Text:
Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: SC Tuesday refused to entertain former Delhi mayor Farhad Suri's plea for an FIR against UP police for conducting a midnight raid at his city home in search of journalist and Ram temple donation pilferage whistleblower Abhishek Upadhyay.Suri's counsel, Anoop Awasthi, told SC that a Ghaziabad police team had raided Suri's Nizamuddin East residence on the night of Aug 22 without disclosing warrants and corresponding entries at Nizamuddin police station. He urged the CJI Surya Kant-led bench to lay down guidelines for the police department of a state conducting midnight raids in another state.UP additional advocate general Sharan Dev Singh Thakur said Suri's petition was an abuse of the process of law and "unnecessary sensationalisation" as police merely rang the bell to find out whether Upadhyay, who was wanted in a road rage case in Ghaziabad, was available at his place. They left after Suri denied Upadhyay's presence, Thakur said, adding that Suri could approach senior police officers for registration of an FIR and, if dissatisfied, he could move a trial court with a private complaint against police.As Suri wanted the FIR to be lodged in Delhi, the bench disposed of his petition by giving him liberty to approach the Nizamuddin police station for filing a complaint against the officers who raided his home unauthorisedly. SC had on Aug 25 protected Upadhyay against arrest by Ghaziabad police. tnn
Article Summary: Suri's counsel told SC that a Ghaziabad police team had raided Suri's Nizamuddin East residence on the night of Aug 22. He urged the CJI Surya Kant-led bench to lay down guidelines for the police department of a state conducting midnight raids.

Article Title: If BJP wins Nagaon, party will secure all 126 Assam seats in 2031: Himanta Biswa Sarma
Article Text:
If BJP wins Nagaon, party will secure all 126 Assam seats in 2031: Himanta Biswa Sarma

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarm on Tuesday made a big claim that BJP could win all 126 assembly seats in the state in the 2031 Vidhan Sabha elections if it wins the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll scheduled for October 6.Speaking at a presser, BJP leader Sarma said Nagaon has not traditionally been a BJP stronghold but claimed that the party has seen a "visible change" in its favour over the past month.The Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency has eight assembly segments. Sarma said the BJP won four of them -- Morigaon, Raha, Jagiroad and Nagaon-Batadraba -- by around 50,000 votes each in the 2026 assembly polls. The opposition won the remaining four -- Rupohihat, Laharighat, Dhing and Samaguri -- by margins of more than 1.5 lakh votes each."Let us wait for the bypoll results... If the BJP manages to win this Lok Sabha seat, then the party will secure all 126 assembly constituencies in the 2031 polls," he said.Sarma said the political mood in the constituency was shifting towards the BJP and claimed the party’s position was improving with each passing day."Even before the elections were announced, many people joined the BJP even in constituencies where we do not have MLAs," he added.Asked about the opposition’s prospects, the chief minister said his focus was on the BJP-led alliance rather than individual opposition leaders."I am not interested in either AIUDF's Badruddin Ajmal or Congress's Gaurav Gogoi but only in the BJP-AGP-BPF alliance. We will continue to do good work and people will be in our favour."However, Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi expressed confidence that the party would win the upcoming Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election, saying the Congress would mount a strong campaign.Speaking to reporters, Gogoi said, "We are very confident of putting up a solid campaign, and we are confident of a victory in the forthcoming Nagaon by-election."Reacting to reports that AIUDF may field its president Badruddin Ajmal in the bypoll, Gogoi said the move reflected the Congress’ strong position in the constituency.He claimed the BJP had been rattled after the Congress announced its candidate and alleged that Ajmal was being brought into the contest to support Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma The BJP has fielded former IAS officer Debashish Sharma for the bypoll, while the Congress has nominated former MLA Sibamoni Bora. Three-time AIUDF MP Badruddin Ajmal is also contesting the seat.Polling for the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll will be held on October 6, while counting is scheduled for April 9.The seat fell vacant after Congress leader Pradyut Bordoloi, who had won Nagaon in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, joined the BJP and won the Dispur assembly seat in this year’s state polls.
Article Summary: If BJP wins Nagaon, party will secure all 126 Assam seats in 2031: Himanta Biswa Sarma. Polling for the Naga on October 6, while counting is scheduled for April 9. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi expressed confidence that the party would win.

Article Title: 'Political conspiracy': Sena (UBT) slams CBI for mentioning Thackerays in FIR on Salian case
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut claims a political conspiracy targets the Thackeray family

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Tuesday alleged that mentioning Aaditya Thackeray in the CBI's FIR in the Disha Salian death case is part of a "political conspiracy" to tarnish the image of the Thackeray family.Speaking to reporters, Raut said Mumbai Police had already investigated the death of Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, and had cleared Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray of any connection with the case.“The way the matter was taken to court, which gave an order (to hand over the case to CBI), is a conspiracy. It has specifically said to conduct a CBI probe but do not name anyone. Yet names are being taken in the media,” Raut told reporters."This is a political conspiracy by Delhi to tarnish the image of the Thackeray family, which enjoys a place in the hearts of people," he added.He also claimed that the CBI probe was being used to target Aaditya Thackeray, who has been critical of the Devendra Fadnavis-led Maharashtra government on several public issues.Raut further alleged that the CBI FIR was being selectively leaked to the media. Referring to the 16-page FIR, he claimed that only one page had been shared.The Shiv Sena (UBT) leader also accused the Centre of previously running campaigns against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, the DMK, Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and former Odisha chief minister Naveen Patnaik.He alleged that a similar campaign was now being directed at the Thackeray family amid the ongoing Supreme Court case concerning the bow-and-arrow symbol allotted to the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena."The case has reached a turning point and someone is scared," Raut said, claiming that an impartial verdict could alter Maharashtra's political landscape and bring the Thackeray family back to centre stage.On September 2, the Bombay high court ordered a CBI probe into Salian's death and criticised Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years. The court observed that the police investigation raised more questions than answers.On Monday, the CBI registered an FIR into Salian's death without naming any accused, in compliance with the Bombay High Court's directions on a petition filed by her father.The FIR content, however, mentions several people, including Aaditya Thackeray, Dino Morea and Rhea Chakraborty, saying their roles need to be probed.On Monday, the central probing agency registered an FIR into Salian's death, naming Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, actors Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, Aaditya's bodyguards, Rhea Chakraborty, Showik Chakraborty, former police officer Sachin Vaze, former Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh, DCP Vishal Thakur and former Maharashtra chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, in compliance with the Bombay High Court's directions on a petition filed by her father.Salian, 28, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 12th floor of a residential building in Mumbai's Malad area. Mumbai Police registered an accidental death report and later said its inquiry had concluded that she had died by suicide.A week later, Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence on June 14, 2020. The proximity of the two deaths led to speculation about a possible connection between them.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut claims a political conspiracy targets the Thackeray family. Raut said Mumbai Police had already investigated the death of Salian, the former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput. He also claimed that the CBI probe was being used to target Aaditya Thackersay.

Article Title: Mumbai slumdweller poses as engineer on matrimonial site, rapes doctor
Article Text:
Police tracked down and arrested Satpute from his residence in a slum pocket in Nalasopara, said inspector Gorakhnath Jaid.





VASAI: Waliv police on Monday arrested a slumdweller from Nalasopara for allegedly raping a 30-year-old doctor from Vasai after posing as an engineer on a matrimonial website and tricking her into meeting him while pretending to be a ‘playboy’.The accused, identified as Subhash Satpute (34), contacted the complainant posing as Kumar Jadhav, an engineer earning Rs 37 lakh annually, on a matrimonial website in June.The doctor liked his profile and agreed to consider the proposal. The accused allegedly told her that she would have to have a physical relationship with a ‘playboy’ to test her sexual compatibility before marriage.Police said Satpute provided her with a phone number and told her to meet the ‘playboy’ at a hotel. She met the man, recorded a video of the sexual act, and sent it to the accused, as instructed.Later, Satpute allegedly refused to marry her, claiming that if he married her, he would die within three months. The woman later learnt that the ‘playboy’ was Satpute.She approached Waliv police, who registered a case under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rape and cheating as well as under the Information Technology Act. Police tracked down and arrested Satpute from his residence in a slum pocket in Nalasopara, said inspector Gorakhnath Jaid.Police said they found that Satpute had created multiple fake Instagram accounts.
Article Summary: The accused, identified as Subhash Satpute (34), contacted the complainant posing as Kumar Jadhav, an engineer earning Rs 37 lakh annually, on a matrimonial website in June. The accused allegedly told her that she would have to have a physical relationship with a ‘playboy’ to test her sexual compatibility.

Article Title: 21-year-old wins first election debut in Jahazpur; 8-time veteran grandpa loses
Article Text:
A 21-year-old physiotherapy student made her electoral debut a winning one in Jahazpur





BHILWARA: A 21-year-old physiotherapy student made her electoral debut a winning one in Jahazpur, while her grandfather, a veteran leader who had won eight times, suffered defeat in the municipality elections whose results were declared Monday.Saniya Khanam, granddaughter of veteran leader Nazir Mohammad, won from Ward 6 as an independent, defeating BJP ’s Mamta Pancholi. A physiotherapy student in Kota, Khanam is the youngest councillor in Bhilwara district.In Ward 16, her grandfather Nazir Mohammad, president of the Anjuman Committee, lost to independent candidate Raees KGN. He had won the ward eight times, including three times on a Congress ticket and four times as an independent. He had also been elected once as a nominated councillor.After filing her nomination, Khanam had said that she was influenced by the Gen Z protest in Delhi to enter the electoral fray. After her victory, she said she was inspired by her grandfather and the movement in Delhi.Khanam said she would raise issues on youth education, a better future, and Jahazpur's development in the municipal board.The results in Jahazpur’s Muslim-majority wards also saw several established faces defeated by newer candidates.
Article Summary: Saniya Khanam won from Ward 6 as an independent, defeating BJP’s Mamta Pancholi. A physiotherapy student in Kota, Khanam is the youngest councillor in Bhilwara district. Her grandfather Nazir Mohammad, president of the Anjuman Committee, lost to independent candidate Raees KGN.

BHAYANDER: Days after an 81-year-old Mira Road resident met his schoolmate, PM Narendra Modi , alleging encroachment of his land in Bhayander by a construction firm owned by BJP MLA Narendra Mehta, the politician said on Tuesday that he is giving up possession of the disputed land and surrendering the nod for construction granted to him for the plot.Mehta also said he was withdrawing a complaint he had earlier filed against the elderly man, Asgar Ali Vora.Vora studied with Modi at B N School in Vadnagar, Gujarat. A meeting was convened at Mantralaya on Tuesday by Shrikar Pardeshi, principal secretary to the CM. Vora, Mehta, Mira-Bhayander municipal commissioner Radha Binod Sharma and town planner Purushottam Shinde attended it.During the meeting, Mehta submitted a letter to the town planning department stating that he was giving up possession of the disputed land and surrendering the construction permission granted. Article Summary: Asgar Ali Vora, 81, alleges encroachment of his land in Bhayander by a construction firm owned by BJP MLA Narendra Mehta. Article Title: Tamil Nadu police book DMK leaders A Raja, PK Sekar Babu over remarks against CM Vijay
Article Text:
DMK leaders A Raja and P K Sekar Babu





CHENNAI: Police have registered cases under various legal provisions against senior DMK leaders A Raja and P K Sekar Babu over alleged defamatory remarks against Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay during recent party demonstrations, an official said on Tuesday.Besides DMK deputy general secretary Raja and former minister Babu, a case was also registered against party MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan for allegedly making defamatory remarks on September 12.The official said a case was registered at B1 North Beach Police Station against Babu, the DMK's Harbour MLA and Chennai East district secretary, following a complaint that he had made derogatory remarks against the chief minister during a party protest.Saidapet police registered a case against Raja based on a complaint filed by TVK functionary Karthik, alleging that Raja made derogatory remarks against Energy Resources and Law Minister R Nirmal Kumar during the protest against the chief minister's speech in the Assembly.Daring the ruling TVK to book a case against him, Raja had said even Congress and BJP leaders had accepted party president M K Stalin's contribution and arrest under MISA during the Emergency.In Kallakurichi, police registered a case against Rishivandhiyam MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan for allegedly making derogatory remarks against Vijay.The DMK had organised statewide protests targeting the chief minister following his remarks on Stalin's detention under MISA during the Emergency and his jaw gestures.While making corruption allegations against the DMK during the recently concluded Assembly session, Vijay referred to Stalin's arrest under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act during the Emergency and made jaw gestures, which were opposed by DMK members in the House.Later, Kumar defended the chief minister's remarks in the Assembly and disputed the long-standing narrative that DMK chief Stalin was arrested under the stringent MISA during the 1975-77 Emergency.Speaking to reporters in Madurai after inspecting preparations for the Meenakshi Amman Temple consecration ceremony, the minister said there was no official detention order copy to substantiate Stalin's claim of being a MISA detainee."No detention copy, no MISA arrest," Kumar had said, accusing the opposition DMK of overreacting and attempting to project Stalin as a political martyr based on unverified historical claims."The fundamental question is whether he was detained under MISA or not," Kumar stated."If anyone is arrested under such an act, there will always be a formal detention order copy. Does Stalin or the DMK have that detention copy? He will end up being the only martyr without one," the minister had said.
Article Summary: Police have registered cases against senior DMK leaders A Raja and P K Sekar Babu over alleged defamatory remarks against Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay. The DMK had organised statewide protests targeting the chief minister following his remarks on Stalin's detention during the Emergency and his jaw gestures.

Article Title: CJP protest: Delhi HC declines PIL seeking fact-finding into conflicting claims over police action
Article Text:
The petition sought directions to the authorities to consider a representation seeking a fact-finding exercise into the alleged lathi-charge and the differing accounts that followed.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has declined to entertain a PIL seeking a fact-finding inquiry into conflicting accounts over the alleged use of lathis by Delhi Police during a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest in the national capital.A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia observed that PIL jurisdiction was not meant to adjudicate such a dispute, particularly when the alleged conflict was based on media reports and official statements.The petition sought directions to the authorities to consider a representation seeking a fact-finding exercise into the alleged lathi-charge and the differing accounts that followed.During the hearing, the Bench questioned whether there was any actual conflict between the official statements of the Delhi Police and the Central Armed Police Forces. The Court also observed that media reports alone cannot be treated as evidence.The Bench observed, "Is there any conflict between the official statements of the Delhi Police and the Central Police Forces? We will not entertain such petitions."The plea was filed by a person claiming to belong to the media community, who had approached the High Court after reports and videos circulated in connection with the CJP protest.The issue relates to the CJP’s protest at Jantar Mantar in July 2026 over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination.During the protest, supporters allegedly attempted to march towards Parliament after gathering at Jantar Mantar. Reports and videos from the spot showed police personnel using force, including lathis and tear gas, to disperse protesters as the situation escalated.At the same time, Delhi Police publicly rejected reports of sporadic violence and detentions at the protest site, saying no such incident had taken place and that the protest was being handled professionally.Subsequent reports carried protesters’ allegations of a lathi-charge and excessive use of force, while police maintained that its action was in response to the situation at the site.The controversy later also reached the High Court in a separate proceeding, where Delhi Police agreed to acknowledge a complaint alleging use of force, including lathis and pellet guns, during the July 20 demonstration.The allegations in the complaint remained subject to consideration and, by themselves, could not establish that the alleged acts had occurred.
Article Summary: The petition sought directions to the authorities to consider a representation seeking a fact-finding exercise into the alleged lathi-charge and the differing accounts that followed. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia observed that PIL jurisdiction was not meant to adjudicate such a dispute.

Article Title: Speeding SUV hits bike in Vashi, 3 youths injured; driver traced
Article Text:
Accused driver of SUV Mahindra Thar escaping after accident





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday.The incident took place around 1am. The injured youths were initially taken to NMMC Hospital in Vashi and were later referred to Sion Hospital for further treatment.Following the incident, a biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police then traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number.During the investigation, it was learnt that the owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride. Police subsequently traced his mobile tower location to an area near the creek in Sector 12, Vashi, where he was allegedly hiding.He was detained and served a notice under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), following which he was released.
Article Summary: Three youths riding a bike were injured after a speeding SUV allegedly hit them head-on near PKC Hospital in Sector 14, Vashi, in the early hours of Monday. A biker passing through the area chased the SUV and recorded its registration number on his mobile phone. Police traced the vehicle's owner and obtained his mobile number. The owner's younger brother had taken the SUV out for a joy ride.

Article Text:
A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel police after an inspection (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 27-year-old quack doctor was detained by Panvel taluka police after a complaint was lodged by the medical officer of the Primary Health Centre at Ajivali village in Panvel taluka, following an inspection by health department officials at his illegal clinic in Kasalkhand village on Monday afternoon.The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal and resides in an MHADA building in India Bulls Township, Kon village, Panvel.Gajanan Ghadge, senior inspector of Panvel taluka police, informed that the complaint was lodged by medical officer Dr Sayali Mankar, 33, who inspected Haq's clinic in Kasalkhand village and found that he was an unqualified and unregistered medical practitioner allegedly practising modern medicine by posing as a doctor.He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.Inspector Ghadge said, "We have invoked relevant sections of the Maharashtra Medical Practitioners Act, 1961, against the accused, which prohibit any person from practising medicine in the state unless their name is registered under the relevant statutory provisions and prescribe criminal penalties and fines for those who illegally practise medicine without valid registration. Under the law, the accused was served a notice under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directing him to appear for inquiry when summoned and during the court proceedings. "
Article Summary: The accused was identified as Noorul Huda Imamul Haq, who hails from West Bengal. He had been running the clinic and treating patients for the past one month, police said. The police seized medicines stocked at the clinic as evidence.

Article Title: 'Grabbed hand and attempted to disrobe': Cab driver tries to assault woman passenger near Navi Mumbai airport
Article Text:
Police have registered a case and are searching for the accused driver (Representative image)





NAVI MUMBAI: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver who took the vehicle to a deserted road near Navi Mumbai airport late on Saturday night, police said on Sunday.The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport, police said. The accused allegedly stopped the cab on the pretext of drinking water before moving to the rear seat beside the woman, police said.According to the police, the woman was travelling to Panvel after a friend booked a cab for her following the party."The driver stopped the vehicle on the deserted service road, stepped out briefly, and then re-entered the car, sitting on the rear seat next to the woman. He allegedly grabbed her hand and attempted to disrobe her," said an official of the Navi Mumbai Police.The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.After the incident, the woman contacted her family and went to Panvel Police Station to lodge a complaint.Since the alleged incident took place within the jurisdiction of Navi Mumbai airport police station, Panvel police escorted her to the appropriate police station.Based on her complaint, Navi Mumbai Airport Police registered a case against the accused, identified as Mohammad Afzal Shaikh, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police have launched a search for Shaikh and are using technical intelligence to trace his whereabouts.Further investigation is underway.(With ANI inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A woman passenger travelling home after attending a party in Chembur allegedly faced molestation and an attempted assault by a cab driver. The incident took place around 1.30am on the airport service road, about two kilometres from Navi Mumbai airport. The woman managed to break free and escape from the vehicle, following which the driver allegedly fled the spot.

Article Title: Palghar hospital assault case: MLA Rajendra Gavit's son, 9 Govindas arrested
Article Text:
The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.





PALGHAR: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of MLA Rajendra Gavit, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar.9 other Govindas were also arrested in the case. The accused were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded them in police custody till September 13.The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations, when local Shiv Sena functionaries allegedly created a ruckus at Relief Hospital over the treatment of injured Govindas.They allegedly assaulted a hospital employee and took away five injured Govindas who were admitted to the ICU.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe and city chief Rahul Gharat.So far, only Gharat had been arrested, while the other accused were absconding. Police had launched a search for them.On Friday, police arrested Rohit Gavit from his residence in Mira Road. According to police, Gavit had obtained a new SIM card and inserted it into his old mobile phone.This helped police trace his location through technical surveillance and arrest him.Police also arrested nine other accused who were among the Govindas involved in the case. They were produced before the Palghar sessions court, which remanded all the accused in police custody till September 13.
Article Summary: Palghar police on Friday arrested Rohit Gavit, son of an MLA, in connection with the assault and ruckus at Relief Hospital in Palghar. The incident took place in the early hours of Saturday, September 5, during the Dahi Handi celebrations. Police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena chief Kundan Sankhe and Rahul Gharat.

Article Title: Intoxicated motorcycle rider disrupts Union minister Mohol’s convoy
Article Text:
Pune:





A drunk motorcycle rider, aged 32, allegedly drove his two-wheeler recklessly into the path of Union minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol’s moving convoy on JM Road, near Sancheti Chowk, around 8.30pm on SundayThe minister’s police guard, assistant police sub-inspector Ishwar Bhikule, lodged a complaint with the Shivajinagar police on Monday who registered a case against the accused for driving under the influence of alcohol and rash driving and served him a notice. Bhikule is posted at the Pune police headquarters.Senior inspector Girish Dighavkar said, “The convoy was heading towards Kothrud from Sancheti Hospital Chowk when the incident occurred."Sirens were being sounded from the vehicles in Mohol’s convoy to alert other motorists. But the accused (from Nana Peth) recklessly drove his motorcycle very close to the convoy and caused an obstruction of movement for some time, police said.Dighavkar said, “The motorcycle rider works as a salesman at a clothing store in the Camp area. After finishing work on Sunday, he had a party with his friends and was returning home. He fled after the incident but we tracked him down after studying CCTV footage. We found him to be intoxicated.”
Article Summary: A drunk motorcycle rider, aged 32, allegedly drove his two-wheeler recklessly into the path of Union minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol’s moving convoy on JM Road, near Sancheti Chowk, around 8.30pm on Sunday. The minister's police guard, assistant police sub-inspector Ishwar Bhikule, lodged a complaint.

Article Title: Auto driver arrested for threatening, assaulting cops in Yercaud
Article Text:
Representative image





SALEM: The Yercaud police have arrested an autorickshaw driver on charges of assaulting a special sub-inspector (SSI) and threatening to kill the SSI and a woman police constable.The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. Yuvraj, who was drunk, obstructed vehicles near a Vinayagar statue on Monday. Head constable D Thavamani, who was regulating traffic, intervened. Yuvraj abused her verbally.SSI Aaron Athirubaraj attempted to defuse the situation. “But Yuvraj tore my shirt, struck me on the chest and threatened to kill me and Thavamani,” the SSI said.Police registered a case against Yuvraj under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation. He was remanded in judicial custody.
Article Summary: The arrested auto driver has been identified as Yuvraj, 22, of Mundagampadi. He was remanded in judicial custody. Police registered a case against him under sections relating to obstructing govt servants, assault and criminal intimidation.

Article Title: Six arrested for murdering fellow guest worker in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Coimbatore:





Six guest workers were arrested on Wednesday, in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district on Monday.Chettipalayam police have identified the arrested as Tuithe Reang, 22, Sunil Rai Reang, 24, Kotho Ram Reang, 30, Sumit Kumar, 20, Sramit Trang, 35, and Santhosh Kumar, 20, all from Tripura.The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit near Othakkalmandapam within Chettipalayam police station limits. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.Investigation revealed that the deceased and the accused were working as housekeeping staff in a private college near Othakkalmandapam. On Monday night they had all consumed alcohol together, and an altercation broke out when the accused asked Badal Shit for money to buy more alcohol, and he refused.“During the altercation, the accused beat him, and Badal Shit died of the severe injuries he suffered in the assault. They then buried him and fled,” said an officer.All six were produced before the judicial magistrate and remanded in custody.
Article Summary: Six guest workers were arrested in connection with the murder of a fellow guest worker near Othakkalmandapam in Coimbatore district. The crime came to light on Tuesday, when an unidentified man’s body was found buried in a pit. A case was registered and the deceased was eventually identified as Badal Shit, 24, from West Bengal.

Article Title: Dharapuram bypoll: ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan first to file nomination
Article Text:
K Padmarajan filling his nomination





TIRUPUR: Filing of nominations for the Dharapuram reserved (scheduled caste) assembly bypoll in Tirupur district began at 11am on Wednesday, with self-styled “Election King” K Padmarajan becoming the first candidate to submit papers before revenue divisional officer A Felix Raja. He is contesting as an independent candidatePadmarajan, a tyre shop owner from Attur in Salem district, said this was his 256th nomination since 1988, filed in Tamil Nadu and other states to underline that ordinary citizens could also contest elections. He claimed that the effort was also part of a Guinness record attempt, adding that he had previously contested against leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, former chief ministers J Jayalalithaa, M Karunanidhi and MK Stalin, and chief minister C Joseph Vijay. He had spent lakhs of rupees on filing nominations over the years.According to the election schedule, nominations can be filed till Sept 16. Scrutiny will be held on Sept 17, and the last date for withdrawal is Sept 19. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.The Dharapuram constituency has been a reserved seat since 1967. The constituency has seen shifting electoral outcomes in recent cycles, with AIADMK winning in 2011, Congress in 2016 and DMK in 2021, before the seat returned to AIADMK in the last assembly election.It is for the first time that a bypoll is going to be held in Tirupur district, which was formed in 2009. The bypoll has been necessitated by the resignation of R Sathyabama, who was the sitting MLA. Sathyabhama, who contested on behalf of AIADMK, won the election from Dharapuram constituency by securing 81,100 votes. She voted in support of the TVK during the floor test in the assembly and subsequently resigned from her MLA post and joined the TVK.Meanwhile, DMK on Wednesday announced S Suganya,33, a lawyer and party women’s wing functionary, as its candidate in the constituency.
Article Summary: Self-styled ‘Election King’ K Padmarajan became the first candidate to submit papers. He said this was his 256th nomination since 1988. Polling is slated for Oct 6, and counting will be held on Oct 9.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu shop owner arrested over banner showing Lord Ganesha eating biryani
Article Text:
Based on the complaint, the Tirunelveli city police commenced an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth





MADURAI: Tirunelveli city police on Saturday arrested a biryani shop owner on allegations that a banner depicted Lord Ganesha eating biryani.According to the complainant, Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that he had noticed that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.He also alleged that the banner was put up with an intention to insult the religious sentiments of Hindus.Based on the complaint, Tirunelveli city police began an inquiry and arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar.He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings.
Article Summary: Tirunelveli city police arrested Jeyanth, 30, of KTC Nagar. He was arrested under Section 299 of the BNS for allegedly committing deliberate and malicious acts intended to outrage religious feelings. Selvaraj, 42, of Narasinganallur, alleged that the banner outside the ‘Dindigul Kalyana Biryani’ shop showed Lord Ganesha eating biryani.

Article Title: Pala civic body vice-chairperson election on today
Article Text:
Kottayam

:





The election of a new vice-chairperson of Pala municipality has been scheduled for 11am in the council hall on Wednesday.Biju Mathews will contest as the nominee of Nagara Vikasana Munnani, a grouping formed by LDF along with dissident Congress councillors, following a decision taken late Monday. UDF’s official candidate will be Sebastian J Panaykkal from Congress.LDF parliamentary party approved Mathews’ candidature at a meeting on Monday. Nagara Vikasana Munnani convener Biju Palooppadavil said the front had agreed to accept a candidate jointly proposed by the four dissident Congress councillors, and Mathews was the choice.The 26-member council has 12 LDF councillors and nine from UDF. Nagara Vikasana Munnani, comprising LDF, the four dissident councillors and chairperson Maya Rahul — who was elected as an independent — has been running the municipal administration together.
Article Summary: The election of a new vice-chairperson of Pala municipality has been scheduled for 11am in the council hall on Wednesday. Biju Mathews will contest as the nominee of Nagara Vikasana Munnani. UDF’s official candidate will be Sebastian J Panaykkal from Congress.

Article Title: Case against bus staff for threatening couple at Edakochi
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Palluruthy Police on Tuesday registered a case against the driver and cleaner of a private bus on charges of verbally abusing and threatening a 55-year-old woman and her 65-year-old husband, during an altercation at a petrol pump in Edakochi.According to the police, the incident occurred around 9pm on Aug 22. The bus driver allegedly stopped the vehicle in front of the couple’s car, which was at the pump for refuelling.When the husband, who is a retired cop, asked the driver to move the bus back, the latter moved the bus in a manner that prevented the car from proceeding. The driver and the cleaner then hurled abusive words at the couple and threatened them.
Article Summary: The incident occurred around 9pm on Aug 22. The bus driver allegedly stopped the vehicle in front of the couple’s car, which was at the pump for refuelling. When the husband, who is a retired cop, asked the driver to move the bus back, the latter moved the bus in a manner that prevented the car from proceeding.

Article Title: Muttil tree-felling: Kerala HC refuses to stay proceedings in cheating case
Article Text:
Kerala High Court

Kochi:





The high court has dismissed a petition filed by Roji Augustine, the prime accused in the Muttil mass tree-felling case in Wayanad, seeking to stay further proceedings in a connected cheating case pending before the Chottanikkara magistrate court until the final report is filed in the mass tree-felling case.While dismissing the petition, a bench of Justice C S Dias directed the Chottanikkara trial court to commence the trial on Sept 22 and dispose of the case within six months. The case pending before the Chottanikkara magistrate court arose from a complaint filed by M M Aliyar of Karimukal in Ernakulam, alleging that he paid Rs 1.40 crore for timber after Augustine claimed that he had valid forest permissions. Although 54 timber logs were delivered with a Form-IV pass, the required permit under the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth on Non-Forest Land Rules, 2006, was not furnished. The timber was later seized, and a case was registered under the Kerala Forest Act and Transit Rules.Another case was registered against Augustine and his brothers for the alleged illegal mass felling of trees in the Meppadi forest range in Wayanad. That case is pending before the Sultan Bathery magistrate court. According to Augustine, the two cases were intrinsically intertwined and proceedings under the Land Conservancy Act would establish that the timber was not forest produce.He contended that proceeding with the cheating case before the forest investigation was concluded would prejudice him.The prosecution opposed the plea, submitting that the petitioner was a history-sheeter accused in 37 similar crimes and that the cases arose from different police stations and involved distinct offences.The court accepted the prosecution’s contention and dismissed the petition. Additionally, the court vacated its earlier order restraining the filing of the final report in a case related to the Muttil mass tree-felling incident, enabling the investigating officer to submit the final report before the Sultan Bathery magistrate court. The court also directed the investigating officer in the Meppadi forest range case to file the final report by Sept 18 for further proceedings.
Article Summary: Roji Augustine, the prime accused in the Muttil mass tree-felling case in Wayanad, sought to stay further proceedings in a connected cheating case pending before the Chottanikkara magistrate court. Augustine claimed that proceeding with the cheating case before the forest investigation was concluded would prejudice him.
